Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the margin you want, the lowest price of a visit, the pay of a cleaner, the extra cost on pay, supplies and travel.
Check Services, Add-ons, Frequency Factors and Areas: these four small tables drive every quote. A labour hour is one cleaner working for one hour; the rate is what you charge for it.
Check Rate Card: the price, hours and cleaners for every service and size band. The price per m2, the price per labour hour and the margin fill in by themselves.
Enter every quote on Quotes. The hours, the price at the rate card, the discount, the margin, the monthly value and the follow-up check fill in by themselves. Open quotes with no follow-up turn red.
Use Site Visits, Office Quotes, Move-out Quotes and Post-construction Quotes for the jobs that need a measure or an estimate. A crew is the cleaners who work together on a job.
Write every follow-up on Quote Follow-ups and every reason a quote was lost on Lost Quotes. Read the price gap and the competitor type to decide where to be cheaper or not.
Keep Clients current. The rate card check shows who pays less than the rate card, and the review check shows who has not had a price review for 12 months.
Write every price change on Price Changes; the change in percent, the start date and the gain per month fill in. Send the letter from the printable documents.
Log market price checks and price tests. A price test is kept only if the win rate times the new price earns more than before.

Use the 14 calculators before you quote: area quote, room quote, frequency price, add-ons, office, move-out, post-construction, travel, minimum price, margin, discount limit, yearly increase, win rate and a what-if grid.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text already written (28 messages).
